title: PAnDA: Combating Negative Augmentation via Large Language Models for User Cold-Start Recommendations
authors: Du, Y.; Chen, R.; Zhao, X.; Han, Q.; Qin, A. K.
venue: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM '25)
tldr: PAnDA framework uses LLMs for preference-aligned and downstream-model-aware data augmentation to address negative augmentation in cold-start recommendation.
problem_and_motivation: Existing LLM-based cold-start augmentation methods suffer from negative augmentation: incomplete augmentation and inaccurate augmentation, stemming from inability to incorporate collaborative signals and lack of awareness of downstream model learning dynamics.
approach: Proposes PAnDA with model-agnostic preference-aligned augmentation module using LLMs as Textual Information Augmentor (TIA).
User-user preference matching and user-item preference coherence generate diverse augmented interactions.
Meta Masked Autoencoder (MetaMAE) with bi-level meta-optimization for personalized collaborative signal augmentation.
Model-specific downstream-model-aware adaptation filters augmented samples using gradient similarity.
Evaluated on MovieLens-1M, Netflix, and Book-Crossing with all-ranking evaluation (Recall@K, NDCG@K, Precision@K).
findings: num: PAnDA consistently outperforms all baselines (BPR, LightGCN, DropoutNet, CL4SRec, L2Aug, KAR, LLMRec, TDAS, M2EU).
Preference-aligned and downstream-model-aware augmentation generates higher quality augmented data.
Adaptive gradient-based filtering outperforms loss-based filtering for augmented sample selection.
key_figures_tables: Figure 1: Illustration of data augmentation methods in cold-start recommendation → Shows negative augmentation problem.
Figure 2: PAnDA architecture → TIA, CSA, and downstream-model-aware filtering components.
Table 2: Experimental results → PAnDA achieves best results across all datasets.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper identifies and formalizes the concept of negative augmentation in cold-start recommendation. It introduces a decoupled framework that separates preference alignment from downstream-model-awareness, enabling flexible LLM and recommendation model combinations. The bi-level meta-optimization strategy for personalized data augmentation advances generative augmentation for recommender systems.
directly_justifies: More augmented data does not necessarily lead to better recommendation performance.
Augmented data must be preference-aligned and downstream-model-aware.
Gradient similarity is more reliable than loss for filtering augmented samples.
limits: Focuses on user cold-start, not item cold-start scenarios.
Not evaluated in personal finance or spending data domains.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 topic domains. Flagged 5.B (high) for cold-start focus, 14.A (high) for synthetic data generation, 6.B (contextual) for prediction modeling, 4.A (contextual) for landscape review. Rejected 1.A-2.D, 7.A-7.E, 8.A-8.C, 9.A-9.C, 10.A-10.C, 11.A-11.B, 12.A-12.C, 13.A-13.C, 14.C. Paper focuses on algorithmic cold-start recommendation, not personal finance.

limitations: Limited to user cold-start scenarios; item cold-start not addressed.
Bi-level optimization may face scalability challenges for large user bases.
Dependence on LLM quality and base recommender candidate set quality.
remember_this: Identifies negative augmentation in cold-start recommendation.
LLMs generate preference-aligned augmented data guided by collaborative signals.
Gradient similarity filters model-mismatched augmented interactions.
PAnDA outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on three benchmark datasets.
